source.title: Dr. No: Feature Steering for Abstention in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Farid Hasanov; Riccardo Renzulli; Bahram Zonooz; Mykola Pechenizkiy; D. Mocanu

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature measurement and steering to real vision-language and language models, reporting evidence about sparse SAE-recoverable features in a new setting. It does not test the toy-model superposition geometry or capacity account.
record.gate_note: Rows are limited to measured SAE-feature separability and held-out answerability detection using the mined feature signal, which bear on V4. The abstention benchmark results for steering, prompting, and other baselines are not rows because they measure abstention performance rather than superposition or feature geometry. The paper also cites prior work on SAE features and steering; those cited results are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper uses off-the-shelf SAEs (LLaVA SAE suite, Qwen-Scope) as a tool to mine abstention and commitment features and steer them. Every reported result is either a feature-selection diagnostic or the performance of its own steering or detection method against baselines. Nothing it measures bears on whether real-model features are superposed, spread across neurons, or recoverable by a dictionary as such. The existence of useful SAE latents is assumed, not tested; no reconstruction quality, feature-recovery or neuron-distribution measure is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Roughly right. The authors conclude that SAE features give lightweight control handles for abstention, improving the answer–abstain trade-off over post-hoc uncertainty baselines on UNK-VQA, incompatibility-type MM-UPD subsets and math AbstentionBench. They find gains are weak on absent-answer detection and MuSiQue. They read this as abstention being governed by source-specific signals rather than one universal direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE feature mining and residual-stream steering for abstention in vision-language and language models; it does not use the toy-network feature-optimization method or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature separability is strongest at later inspected LLaVA layers; held-out signal varies by benchmark and source of unanswerability, with AAD weakest. Steering configuration and strength are benchmark-specific, but those behavioral outcomes are outside the rows for these claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: A few SAE latents at the decision token separate abstain from commit states (layer-24 AUROC 0.998 in-sample). Steering them outperforms random SAE features (UNK-VQA HM 38.7 vs 35.6) and slightly outperforms dense residual steering (38.7 vs 38.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behaviour-linked SAE latents (e.g. epistemic abstention) exist in VLMs/LLMs and act as causal control directions somewhat better than random latents or dense directions.

record.code_released: Will release the Dr. No feature-mining, steering, and evaluation code; URL not stated.
record.problems: The strongest feature separability in Table 5 is measured on the mining corpus after behavioral filtering, not on held-out data. The paper explicitly warns that this is not universal answerability detection. The reported held-out detection values are shown in Figure 2 without uncertainty estimates. The study does not measure superposition geometry, capacity pressure, or feature dimensionality.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V4-relevant rows were omitted. Abstention accuracy and steering results in Tables 2, 3, 6, and 7, as well as ablations and strength sweeps, measure abstention behavior rather than the representation properties named by the tested version.

untested.parts: No toy-model experiment, feature-geometry, sparsity-transition or regular-geometry measurement.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No study of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
Uses pretrained SAEs without measuring superposition, neuron-level feature spread, SAE reconstruction or recovery of ground-truth features.
Mining-seed stability of selected latent IDs (Tables 11–12) uses a fixed SAE. It does not test completeness, canonicality or stability of SAE features across SAE training.
Steers single decoder directions but does not test whether the features are one-dimensional.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/tests classification and V4 'supports' labels are not justified. The paper is an applied steering-method paper, and superposition and SAE validity are presupposed. Its Table 5 values are explicitly labelled a mining diagnostic, and Figure 2 compares its detector with baselines. The Table 13 ablations (random features) and the dense-steering comparison are also method comparisons. They are noted under fits_no_version rather than as V4 evidence.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network superposition experiment, feature-overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry is measured.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Measures selected SAE feature activity and its answerability signal, but does not establish that real-model features are generally spread across neurons or characterize the full representation.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or universally stable units; seed stability of selected feature IDs is not a test of those properties.
Uses individual SAE decoder directions for interventions but does not test whether the represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.operation_detail: Measured AUROC and class-mean activations of the strongest abstention-associated SAE feature at each inspected layer on the GQA mining corpus.
rows.measure: Strongest feature AUROC; mean activation (abstain / commit)
rows.note: Mining-corpus feature separability; not a held-out answerability result.
rows.check: Selection value: AUROC of the best of 32,768 latents, chosen in-sample on a behaviourally filtered mining corpus. The paper calls it a mining diagnostic. It does not measure superposition or SAE recoverability.
